LESSON: COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Comprehension, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What do the pictures tell us about the story? 2. What do you think will happen in the story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication: the learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they retell a story related to the theme.

creativity and imagination: the l e a r n e r p r a c t i s e s m a k i n g c o n n e c t i o n s a s t h e y share their own

experiences in relation to the story

Values:
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as the learner collaboratively discusses care for domestic animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (Animal Welfare Education): The learner acquires information on animal welfare

as they read texts on how to take care of domestic animals.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies reading comprehension skills in reading of texts in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Video clips, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,
